# Repository scan (scan index)

_sequence · source: `docs/atlas/views/sequence/repository-scan.yaml`_

How the catalog learns what is on disk. Scan requests from an administrator, the filesystem watcher, or the periodic timer are only queued rows; one River delivery per repository runs bounded walk turns first and hashes only when no walk is due. Absence is never inferred from a hint.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor n_admin as Administrator (Web)
    participant n_watcher as Filesystem watcher
    participant n_api as RepositoryScanHandler
    participant n_scanner as Scanner
    participant n_catalog as repository_scans / repository_entries
    participant n_scheduler as Catalog scheduler
    participant n_worker as ScanRepositoryBatchWorker
    participant n_disk as Repository files
    participant n_writer as ScanWriter (commit coordinator)
    alt manual verification
        n_admin->>n_api: POST /storage/repositories/{id}/verifications
        n_api->>n_scanner: RequestScan(trigger=manual)
    else filesystem events (batched, 10 s)
        n_watcher->>n_scanner: request a subtree scan, or a full scan above 512 events
    else periodic timer (jittered)
        n_scanner->>n_scanner: RequestAllPeriodic
    end
    n_scanner->>n_catalog: insert or coalesce a queued scan
    n_scheduler->>n_worker: one unique ScanRepositoryBatchArgs per repository
    loop walk turns, up to the delivery budget
        n_worker->>n_scanner: RunTurn
        n_scanner->>n_disk: list one directory completely (sorted, stat cache)
        n_scanner->>n_writer: write only the diff — new, changed (pending_hash), restored, missing
        n_writer->>n_catalog: one bounded transaction per batch (≤ 256 rows)
    end
    Note over n_scanner,n_disk: A catalog-only row becomes missing only after a positive absence probe with the repository marker re-checked#59; an offline repository ends the scan as offline.
    loop hash turns, when no walk is due
        n_worker->>n_scanner: HashTurn (32 pending_hash entries)
        n_scanner->>n_disk: hash outside any transaction
        n_scanner->>n_writer: compare-and-swap on the entry revision, bind content to an Asset
        n_writer->>n_catalog: activation requests the Asset's pipeline stages
    end
    n_worker->>n_scheduler: snooze while more work remains#59; finish records counters
```

## Disk is the truth

The catalog mirrors each repository tree in repository_entries, one row per file or directory. A full scan is the authority; watcher events only make the next scan sooner. Nothing in this flow unlinks, trashes, or purges a file.

## Bounded writer holds

No filesystem I/O, hashing, or sleeping happens inside a catalog transaction. Write batches are at most 256 rows and are sized to stay inside the 25 ms writer-hold budget, so scanning a 40k-file repository never starves foreground requests.
